why: A smaller number wants smaller digits as early as possible, so while the last kept digit is larger than the incoming one and deletions remain, delete it. The kept digits form a non-decreasing stack. It is the canonical 'lexicographically smallest result' monotonic stack.
hints: Comparing two results of the same length, which position decides which one is smaller?
The first position where they differ. So if a kept digit is followed by a smaller one, deleting the larger one is always better.
Stack of kept digits: for each digit, pop while k > 0 and top > digit (k -= 1), then push. If k remains, drop it from the end. Strip leading zeros; return "0" if nothing is left. O(n).
pitfalls: If the digits are non-decreasing ("12345"), no pop happens; remove the remaining k from the end.
Strip leading zeros, and return "0" (not "") for an empty result.
